answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted, randomly audited identities: before bidding, each agent locks collateral in a public ledger, and peers picked by a verifiable random beacon recheck identity and slash the entire stake on any proof of duplicate voting. An attacker wanting N fake agents must post N independent stakes, so cost rises linearly, while one detected forgery burns that node's whole bond and future earnings. Like a rare opal pigment that cannot be mass-produced, or an ocean of open audits, faking many identities costs far more than any single honest reward.
